exposure: Standardized hydrostatic low-volume saline enemas, Manual enemas using varied techniques (control group)
outcome: Gastrointestinal complications (necrotizing enterocolitis [NEC], focal intestinal perforation [FIP], meconium plug syndrome [MPS]), Morbidity, Mortality, Stool parameters, Feeding parameters, Staff evaluations
cohort: Infants with a birth weight <=1000 g or gestational age <=28 weeks and delayed meconium passage, born between January 2019 and October 2022.
finding: Standardized hydrostatic low-volume saline enemas are a safe and effective alternative to conventional rectal interventions, offering improved comfort and potentially reducing intestinal morbidity in infants with very low birth weight or gestational age.
